core.title: Use only registry-declared kebab-case themes on plan-namespace artifacts and contracts
core.given: A plan artifact or contract uses the repository plan theme namespace (a theme declaration or a theme-prefixed identity), or the theme registry is involved.
core.when: You author, edit or review such an artifact, contract or the theme registry.
core.then: Every declared theme must be a value in the repository theme registry (registry membership).
prefer: Add the theme to the registry before any artifact or contract references it.
Required: theme names are kebab-case matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$.
Required: registry index 0 is commons, the only reserved entry; the repository declares every other theme.
Required: the first segment of every artifact or contract identity equals its declared theme.
avoid: Declaring a theme absent from the registry.
Theme names with uppercase, underscores, spaces or leading digits/hyphens.
Removing, renaming or moving commons off index 0, or reserving another entry.
An identity whose first segment differs from its theme.
core.why: A theme is a repository-defined namespace for plan artifacts; registry membership and identity-prefix consistency are what make it enforceable.
evidence: Every plan-namespace theme value on an artifact or contract appears in the registry.
Every registry entry and declared theme matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$.
The registry entry at index 0 is exactly commons.
For each plan-namespace artifact or contract, the first segment of its identity equals its declared theme.
verification: Membership check: every declared theme is a value in the repository theme registry (the registry path is profile data).
Theme-format check: every registry entry and every declared theme matches the required kebab-case format ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$.
Reserved-entry check: the registry entry at index 0 is exactly commons, the only reserved entry; every other entry is repository-declared.
Identity-prefix check: the first segment of a plan-namespace artifact or contract identity equals its declared theme; how identities are segmented follows the stack's identity shapes.
Term model: a theme is a kebab-case namespace with registry membership and an identity prefix; membership and identity-prefix consistency are the enforceable parts of this definition.

Scope: classify by use of the plan theme namespace (plan artifact schema, or a contract identity namespaced by a plan theme), never by a bare 'theme' key; exclude UI and other unrelated theme systems. Default check scope is the artifacts, contracts and registry touched by the change; because the invariants are unconditional, a verifier MAY optionally scan full repository state, but this is a verification strategy, not an authoring duty.

values: a declared theme is absent from the registry
a theme name violates the required format
the registry's reserved first entry is missing, renamed or reordered
an identity's first segment differs from its theme

fires: A plan artifact is created or edited and declares or changes its theme or theme-prefixed identity.
A contract whose identity is namespaced by a plan theme is created or edited, in any part of the repository.
The theme registry is created, or an entry is added, renamed, reordered or removed.
A planner reviews a plan artifact or contract that assigns or references a plan theme.
doesNotFire: Files that do not use the plan theme namespace and are not the theme registry.
UI/visual, editor, documentation-site or any other non-plan theme configuration, even when it declares a theme key or value.
Prose that mentions the word theme in an unrelated sense.

profileRequirements.meaning: Where files of the plan_artifact role live; the primary location of plan-namespace artifacts, used to scope activation.
The concrete plan-artifact kinds in this stack that declare themes or theme-prefixed identities.
The registry file declaring every theme of the repository plan theme namespace; the membership target of the obligation and the reserved-entry check.

proposedKeys.meaning: Path of the repository plan-theme registry file that declares every theme of the plan theme namespace (index 0 reserved).
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: roots.* name top-level trees (roots.plan is only the plan root) and layout.* name wagon/feature/commons/plan-item locations; no key names the theme registry file itself, and the membership obligation and its check need that exact path.

bunOnly.reason: A literal path-glob activation fact is the Bun realization's sensing mechanism; the neutral core senses the theme_registry file kind and takes the registry location from the profile (layout.theme_registry).

bunOnly.reason: The concrete plan-root glob is stack data; the neutral core senses the plan_artifact role and takes its location from the profile (roles.plan_artifact.path).

neutralityNotes: The core names no path: the registry location and the plan-artifact location are profile data (layout.theme_registry, proposed; roles.plan_artifact.path). The reserved index-0 value 'commons' and the kebab-case format ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ are kept in the core because the canonical source defines them as part of the theme-namespace convention itself, not as stack mechanics; a stack that must differ needs an owner decision (a new profile key), not a silent realization change. 'First segment' of an identity depends on the stack's identity (URN) shapes (urn.* keys); the core states only the neutral obligation that it equals the theme. Literal path-glob activation facts and this rule's finding ids remain Bun-only realization details.
